key_insight: Welding innovations can be technically superior yet still take a median 14.5 years to reach production because defects, process trade-offs, and translation barriers slow adoption.
engineering_relevance: The review helps engineers choose welding processes more transparently and highlights where reliability, economics, and code approval most often block deployment.
method: Survival analysis of 31 welding innovations from first demonstration to production
Semi-structured interviews with 23 welding professionals plus reliability testing of diagnostic instruments
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a median lab-to-production translation time of 14.5 years, with innovations that had an organisational owner reaching production faster (11.0 years vs 19.0 years).
watch_item: The proposed heuristics and physics-informed neural-network concept are preliminary, and real-world adoption still depends on economic validation and code submission.
paper_title: Bridging the Welding Lab-to-Shop Gap: Why Proven Innovations Lag — A Review of Defect Persistence, Process Trade-Offs, and Translation Barriers
